name: Maria-Elisabeth Schaeffler-Thumann
name_chinese: 玛丽亚·伊丽莎白·谢弗勒
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: Maria-Elisabeth Schaeffler-Thumann and her billionaire son Georg own Schaeffler Group, one of the world's largest ball bearing and machine component producers.
She took over in 1996, following the death of her husband (also Georg) who had founded the company with his brother Wilhelm in 1946.
In 2008, the company took over tire and auto parts giant Continental AG in a $15-billion, debt-financed deal.
In the wake of the financial crisis, it seemed the high-wire act might fail. But as the auto market rebounded, Continental's share price soared.
Maria-Elisabeth and Georg's combined 46% stake in Continental accounts for most of their wealth.
forbes_facts: Maria-Elisabeth, who owns 20% of Schaeffler Group, lives in the tony Austrian ski resort town of Kitzbuehel, while Georg, with 80%, leads a quiet life in the U.S.
In 2014, she married Juergen Thumann, former head of the German industrial organization BDI.

name: Jed McCaleb
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: An early pioneer in the blockchain space, Jed McCaleb helped launch three well-known crypto firms.
In 2010 he created Mt. Gox, the first major Bitcoin exchange, which he sold a year later before it was hacked.
McCaleb cofounded Ripple in 2012, but soon left over disagreements with fellow founders.
His next venture, in 2014, was cofounding Stellar, a Ripple competitor that aims to speed up cross-border payments.
Most of McCaleb's wealth comes from selling much of the original 9 billion XRP he pocketed as a Ripple cofounder. He sold his last coins in 2022.
forbes_facts: Before entering crypto, McCaleb created the file-sharing service eDonkey2000, which was sued by major record companies over copyright infringement.
McCaleb's separation agreement with Ripple required him to move 2 million XRP tokens to a charitable fund of his choice.

name: Adi Godrej
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Adi Godrej, patriarch of the storied Godrej clan, controls the Godrej Industries Group with his younger brother, Nadir Godrej.
The group consists of four listed companies, Godrej Consumer Products, Godrej Industries, Godrej Properties and Godrej Agrovet.
His brother Nadir is chairman of the group, while his son, Pirojsha is vice chairman.
In 2024, the siblings and their cousins Jamshyd and Smita Crishna-Godrej divided the family's business empire into two separate business groups
forbes_facts: The Godrej group was established by lawyer Ardeshir Godrej, who gave up his profession to make locks in 1897.
Godrej launched the world's first soap made from vegetable oil in 1918.
Godrej aerospace engines were used in India's mission to Mars in 2014.

name: Marc Fielmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Marc Fielmann is the CEO of Fielmann Group AG, Europe's leading optical company that operates stores and online shops across the continent and also in the United States.

Guenther Fielmann handed over the company to his son Marc as the market leader in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland in 2018 with approximately 700 stores. As of now Fielmann operates around 1,300 stores.
With revenues exceeding EUR 2 billion and some 24,000 employees, Fielmann serves more than 28 million customers.
Fielmann holds a BSc from the London School of Economics and Poltical Science (LSE).
He began working at the company in 2012 and took over the reigns from his father in 2019.

name: Jay-Z
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Since becoming hip-hop's first billionaire in 2019, Jay-Z has more than doubled his fortune thanks to his lucrative liquor businesses.
He sold 50% of spirits brand Armand de Brignac, otherwise known as Ace of Spades, to luxury goods giant LVMH in 2021, and sold a majority of his stake in cognac brand D'Usse to Bacardi in 2023.
He is also chairman and cofounder of entertainment company Roc Nation, and has stakes in music streaming giant Tidal and the 40/40 Club sports bar.
His other assets range from a fine art collection including works by Jean-Michel Basquiat, his music catalog and shares in companies like Block and Uber.
He was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame in 2021, and has won two Emmys for Super Bowl halftime shows in 2022 and 2023.
forbes_facts: Jay-Z, with 88, and his wife Beyoncé Knowles, with 99, are the two artists with the most Grammy nominations ever.
Jay-Z was the first rap artist inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, in 2017.
A founding partner of Reform Alliance and board member of the United Justice Coalition, Jay-Z advocates for social justice initiatives and criminal justice reform.

name: Jerry Speyer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Real estate baron Jerry Speyer redeveloped landmarks like Rockefeller Center and the Chrysler Building in Manhattan.
Jerry is the chairman of Tishman Speyer and his son Rob is CEO. Until 2015, they held co-CEO titles.
Tishman Speyer has developed over 152 million square feet, including skyscrapers in New York, Chicago, Berlin, London, Frankfurt and Paris.
Speyer started the firm with his late father-in-law, Robert Tishman, in 1978. The marriage ended in divorce, but the company survived.
forbes_facts: Speyer was chairman of the Museum of Modern Art's board of trustees for 11 years and was elected chairman of New York Presbyterian Hospital in 2018.
Speyer has hundreds of art works in his personal collection, which skews contemporary and includes pieces by Damien Hirst and Andy Warhol.
